1	1
Grammar Summary Part 2
Bac
Habits in the Past
 They used to live in Melbourne.
 When he was young, he used to collect stamps.
 When he was young, he would collect stamps.
 Kelly did not use to smoke in her thirties.
 When he was in kindergarten, Gaston would not go to bed unless his bedroom door was left open.
 When he was in kindergarten, Gaston did not use to go to bed unless his bedroom door was left
open.
Used to + base form
 Past habits.
 Repeated actions in the past.
 Past states.
PS. In the negative form, the verb “used”
becomes “use” without the “d” because the
auxiliary verb “do” is the one to be conjugated
and put in the past.
Would + base form
 Past habits.
 Not used to talk about past
states/with stative verbs such as
love, be, understand, and feel.
 Should not be used unless it has
already been established that the
time frame is in the past.

Grammar Summary Part 2

Habits in the Present
➢ I am used to walking long distances.
➢ Christopher is used to living by himself.
➢ Could you turn down the music? I am not used to listening to loud music.
➢ A: Are the children used to sleeping in the dark?
B: No, the children are not used to sleeping in the dark.
Be (simple present) + used to + verb + ing

Negative Prefixes
You can make negative statements by adding negative prefixes to nouns, adjectives, and verbs.
These prefixes include: il–, im–, ir, in–, dis-, de–, non–, un–, mis–
 Il+ l______ : Legal → Illegal
 Im+ m/p/ b______ : Mature→ Immature Possible → Impossible Balance → Imbalance
 Ir+ r_______: Resistible → Irresistible
 In: Sane → Insane
 Dis: Satisfy → Dissatisfy
 De: Activate → Deactivate
 Non: Sense → Nonsense
 Un: Comfortable → Uncomfortable
 Mis: Understand → Misunderstand
PS. there are some exception though.

Grammar Summary Part 2
Bac
So that vs. So…that
So that So…that
She went to a nearby restaurant so that she could
grab a bite.
• Why did she go to a nearby restaurant?
➔ To grab a bite. → purpose
Akeem is going to London so that he can learn to
speak English more fluently.
• Why is Akeem going to London?
➔ To learn to speak English more fluently. →
purpose
She spoke so faintly that nobody could hear a
word she said.
→ So + adverb + that
• What was the result of speaking faintly?
➔ Nobody could hear a word she said. → Result
The room is so hot that I might pass out.
→So + adjective + that
• What is the result of being so hot?
➔ I might pass out. → Result
➔ So… that express a cause and a consequence.
Emphatic forms
Emphatic forms are made with the auxiliary verb do in the present (do or does) or past tense (did) + the
base form of the verb.
➢ A: She never listens to what her parents say.
B: I don't agree with you; she does listen to what her parents say.
➢ Please, do sit down.
➢ When his boss complained that he did not write the reports he asked him to, Justin raised the
contention that this was inaccurate, as he did hand in all those reports the week before.

6	6
Grammar Summary Part 2
Bac
Showing Contrast
In spite of Despite Although Even though Though
➢ Used to link two contrasting ideas.
➢ They show that one fact makes the other fact surprising.
➢ They can all be used at the beginning or in the middle of the sentence.
 Followed by a noun, gerund (ing
form of a verb), or a pronoun.
 Can be followed by the
expression “the fact that”,
followed by a subject and verb.
In spite of/ despite preparing well for
the interview, Zach did not get the job.
In spite of/ despite the fact that he
prepared well for the interview, Zach
did not get the job.
 Followed by a subject and a verb.
 Even though is slightly stronger and more
emphatic than although.
 Though can also go at the end of the second
phrase. This way of expressing contrasting ideas is
most common in spoken English.
Although/ even though/ though Zach prepared well
for the interview, he did not get the job.
Zach prepared well for the interview; he did not get
the job though.
If Vs. Unless
If Unless
If means on the condition that, provided that,
providing that, presuming that, supposing that,
assuming that, as long as...
Unless means except if or simply if...not.
➢ If you do not go to bed early, you will be late
for school.
➢ She will not be able to hand in the report on
time if we do not help her.
➢ You will fail the exam if you do not study hard.
➢ If you do not hurry up, we will be late.
➔ Unless you go to bed early, you will be late for
school.
➔ She will not be able to hand in the report on
time unless we help her.
➔ You will fail the exam unless you study hard.
➔ Unless you hurry up, we will be late.
If + negative verb = unless + positive verb

These verbs can be followed by a Gerund and an Infinitive without changing their meaning:
Begin/ start/ continue/ cease/ prefer/ propose/ neglect/ attempt/ like, etc.
These verbs can also be followed by a gerund or an infinitive without changing their meaning. Mind
the structure with the infinitive.
Gerund: Verb + –ing
Infinitive: Verb + Person (as object) + to infinitive
Verb Examples
advise They advised going there was a waste of time.
They advise us not to go there as it was a waste of time.
Allow They allow smoking in this café.

9	9
Grammar Summary Part 2
Bac
Encourage I encourage speaking to native speakers.
I encourage you to speak to native speakers.
Forbid They have forbidden hunting here.
They have forbidden people to hunt here.
Permit They do not permit hunting here.
They do not permit people to hunt here.
Some verbs which can take both forms have a change in meaning depending on
whether the verb is followed by the gerund or the infinitive. E.g.:
Verb To + inf Gerund
Forget I forgot to lock the door.
➔ I did not lock the door because I
forgot.
I forgot locking the door.
➔ I do not remember that I locked
the door. I do not remember the
whole scene.
Remember Make sure to remember to pick the
kids up from school.
➔ You should do this action.
➔ Look into the future.
I remember picking the kids up
from school.
➔ I have the memory of doing this
in the past.
Regret I regret to inform you that your
wife passed away.
➔ I must do something unpleasant.
➔ To tell bad news and I am not
happy about it.
I regret telling him my secret. He
told everyone else.
➔ I do not like what I did, so I feel
regretful.
➔ I did something in the past and I
am not happy about it.
Stop I stopped to talk on the phone.
➔ I was driving, and I stopped the
car in order to make a phone call.
→ The reason why I stopped is to
talk on the phone.
I stopped talking on the phone.
➔ I was talking on the phone, and
then I stopped doing that (when I
saw a policeman).
➔ To stop doing the activity.

Grammar Summary Part 2

Try You should try to travel more.
➔ I encourage you to travel.
➔ To do something that is not easy.
Have you ever tried eating sushi?
➔ To experiment, test, or do
something new.
Quit Jason quit to work here.
➔ He quit another job to work here.
Jason quit working here.
➔ He does not work here anymore.
Go on She studied chemistry, then Amy
went on to study Physics.
➔ She studied Chemistry first, then
she studied Physics.
➔ To change the activity.
Amy went on learning Physics.
➔ She continued learning Physics.
➔ To continue with the same thing
Mean I did not mean to hurt your feelings.
➔ I did not intend to hurt your
feelings.
➔ Intend to do something.
Working in a big means leaving
home at a very early hour.
➔ This is the result or consequence.
➔ Something has to be done to get a
result.
Need You really need to get your blood
tested.
➔ If we use a gerund after need,
then the sentence has an active
meaning (have a necessity to do
something).
The car needs cleaning.
➔ If we use a gerund after need,
then the sentence has a passive
meaning (something needs to be
done).
Want I want you to clean the car.
➔ If we use a gerund after want,
then the sentence has an active
meaning (have a necessity to do
something).
The car wants cleaning.
➔ If we use a gerund after want,
then the sentence has a passive
meaning (something needs to be
done).
Dread I dread to think what your Mom is
going to say when she finds out
about your school results.
➔ Not want to do something.
My son really dreads going to the
dentist. It makes him very anxious.
➔ Be scared of doing something.

11	11
Grammar Summary Part 2
Bac
Hate, like, love and prefer can be followed either by -ing or a to-infinitive. The difference in meaning
is often small. The -ing form emphasizes the verb itself. The to-infinitive puts the emphasis more on
the preference for, or the results of, the action.
 I love cooking Italian food. (Emphasis on the process itself and enjoyment of it → Use the
Gerund when like is used in the sense of 'enjoy'.)
 I like to see my doctor twice a year. (Think of it as correct or wise. Emphasis more on the
preference or habit)
 I like to meditate in the morning. (I think, it is good to meditate in the morning. → Use the
Infinitive when you do something as a habit.)
 I hate to be the only who does not understand. (Emphasis more on the result: I would prefer
not to be in that situation.)
 I hate to interrupt, but you really need to take this call. (Be sorry about what you are going to
say or do because you think it is unpleasant or not correct to do.)
 I hate waiting in long lines. (Dislike very much.)
 She hates sweeping the floor. (Emphasis on the process itself and lack enjoyment of it)
 I prefer walking to driving. (Emphasis on the process itself and enjoyment of it)

 I hate waiting in long lines. (Dislike very much.)
 She hates sweeping the floor. (Emphasis on the process itself and lack enjoyment of it)
 I prefer walking to driving. (Emphasis on the process itself and enjoyment of it)

 Repeated actions in the past.
 Past states.

becomes “use” without the “d” because the
auxiliary verb “do” is the one to be conjugated
and put in the past.

 Past habits.
 Not used to talk about past
states/with stative verbs such as
love, be, understand, and feel.

already been established that the
time frame is in the past.

Negative Prefixes
You can make negative statements by adding negative prefixes to nouns, adjectives, and verbs.
These prefixes include: il–, im–, ir, in–, dis-, de–, non–, un–, mis–
 Il+ l______ : Legal → Illegal
 Im+ m/p/ b______ : Mature→ Immature Possible → Impossible Balance → Imbalance
 Ir+ r_______: Resistible → Irresistible
 In: Sane → Insane
 Dis: Satisfy → Dissatisfy
 De: Activate → Deactivate
 Non: Sense → Nonsense
 Un: Comfortable → Uncomfortable
 Mis: Understand → Misunderstand

Grammar Summary Part 2
Bac
So that vs. So…that
So that So…that
She went to a nearby restaurant so that she could
grab a bite.
• Why did she go to a nearby restaurant?
➔ To grab a bite. → purpose
Akeem is going to London so that he can learn to
speak English more fluently.
• Why is Akeem going to London?
➔ To learn to speak English more fluently. →
purpose
She spoke so faintly that nobody could hear a
word she said.
→ So + adverb + that
• What was the result of speaking faintly?
➔ Nobody could hear a word she said. → Result
The room is so hot that I might pass out.
→So + adjective + that
• What is the result of being so hot?
➔ I might pass out. → Result
➔ So… that express a cause and a consequence.
Emphatic forms
Emphatic forms are made with the auxiliary verb do in the present (do or does) or past tense (did) + the
base form of the verb.
➢ A: She never listens to what her parents say.
B: I don't agree with you; she does listen to what her parents say.
➢ Please, do sit down.
➢ When his boss complained that he did not write the reports he asked him to, Justin raised the
contention that this was inaccurate, as he did hand in all those reports the week before.

© TakiAcademy.com
6	6
Grammar Summary Part 2
Bac
Showing Contrast
In spite of Despite Although Even though Though
➢ Used to link two contrasting ideas.
➢ They show that one fact makes the other fact surprising.
➢ They can all be used at the beginning or in the middle of the sentence.
 Followed by a noun, gerund (ing
form of a verb), or a pronoun.
 Can be followed by the
expression “the fact that”,
followed by a subject and verb.
In spite of/ despite preparing well for
the interview, Zach did not get the job.
In spite of/ despite the fact that he
prepared well for the interview, Zach
did not get the job.
 Followed by a subject and a verb.
 Even though is slightly stronger and more
emphatic than although.
 Though can also go at the end of the second
phrase. This way of expressing contrasting ideas is
most common in spoken English.
Although/ even though/ though Zach prepared well
for the interview, he did not get the job.
Zach prepared well for the interview; he did not get
the job though.
If Vs. Unless
If Unless
If means on the condition that, provided that,
providing that, presuming that, supposing that,
assuming that, as long as...
Unless means except if or simply if...not.
➢ If you do not go to bed early, you will be late
for school.
➢ She will not be able to hand in the report on
time if we do not help her.
➢ You will fail the exam if you do not study hard.
➢ If you do not hurry up, we will be late.
➔ Unless you go to bed early, you will be late for
school.
➔ She will not be able to hand in the report on
time unless we help her.
➔ You will fail the exam unless you study hard.
➔ Unless you hurry up, we will be late.
If + negative verb = unless + positive verb

These verbs can be followed by a Gerund and an Infinitive without changing their meaning:
Begin/ start/ continue/ cease/ prefer/ propose/ neglect/ attempt/ like, etc.

Permit They do not permit hunting here.

Some verbs which can take both forms have a change in meaning depending on
whether the verb is followed by the gerund or the infinitive. E.g.:
Verb To + inf Gerund
Forget I forgot to lock the door.
➔ I did not lock the door because I
forgot.
I forgot locking the door.
➔ I do not remember that I locked

whole scene.

➔ Look into the future.

from school.

in the past.

➔ I must do something unpleasant.
➔ To tell bad news and I am not

Grammar Summary Part 2
Bac
Hate, like, love and prefer can be followed either by -ing or a to-infinitive. The difference in meaning
is often small. The -ing form emphasizes the verb itself. The to-infinitive puts the emphasis more on
the preference for, or the results of, the action.
 I love cooking Italian food. (Emphasis on the process itself and enjoyment of it → Use the
Gerund when like is used in the sense of 'enjoy'.)
 I like to see my doctor twice a year. (Think of it as correct or wise. Emphasis more on the
preference or habit)
 I like to meditate in the morning. (I think, it is good to meditate in the morning. → Use the
Infinitive when you do something as a habit.)
 I hate to be the only who does not understand. (Emphasis more on the result: I would prefer
not to be in that situation.)
 I hate to interrupt, but you really need to take this call. (Be sorry about what you are going to
say or do because you think it is unpleasant or not correct to do.)
 I hate waiting in long lines. (Dislike very much.)
 She hates sweeping the floor. (Emphasis on the process itself and lack enjoyment of it)
 I prefer walking to driving. (Emphasis on the process itself and enjoyment of it)
